title: Nondegeneracy of faithful semisimple trace forms
statement:
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field], let $L$ be a finite-dimensional semisimple $F$-Lie algebra [def-wf-lie-algebra, def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra], let $M$ be a finite-dimensional $F$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], and let $\rho:L\to\operatorname{End}_F(M)$ be an injective Lie representation, meaning a linear map with $\rho([x,y])=\rho(x)\rho(y)-\rho(y)\rho(x)$. The symmetric bilinear form, using ordinary trace [def-weil-endomorphism-trace],
$$B_\rho(x,y)=\operatorname{Tr}_M(\rho(x)\rho(y))$$
is nondegenerate: if $B_\rho(x,y)=0$ for all $y\in L$, then $x=0$.

source.place: §22c, printed p.475, The Casimir operator, paragraph applying Cartan criterion to the kernel of the trace form of a faithful representation.

proof.text: By the matrix-diagonal formula for trace [def-weil-endomorphism-trace], trace is $F$-linear. Composition is bilinear, so $B_\rho$ is bilinear. Apply [lem-pc-finite-dimensional-trace-cyclic] to the two endomorphisms $\rho(x),\rho(y)$ of $M$ to obtain $B_\rho(x,y)=B_\rho(y,x)$.

source.place: §22c, printed p.475, The Casimir operator, paragraph applying Cartan criterion to the kernel of the trace form of a faithful representation.

proof.text: Put $R=\{x\in L:B_\rho(x,y)=0\text{ for all }y\in L\}$. Bilinearity makes $R$ a linear subspace. For $z,y\in L$ and $x\in R$, bracket preservation [def-wf-lie-algebra] and trace cyclicity [lem-pc-finite-dimensional-trace-cyclic] give $B_\rho([z,x],y)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho(z)\rho(x)\rho(y)-\rho(x)\rho(z)\rho(y))=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho(x)(\rho(y)\rho(z)-\rho(z)\rho(y)))=B_\rho(x,[y,z])=0$. Here cyclicity moves the first factor $\rho(z)$ of the first triple product to the end. Hence $[L,R]\subseteq R$, so $R$ is an ideal.

source.place: §22c, printed p.475, The Casimir operator, paragraph applying Cartan criterion to the kernel of the trace form of a faithful representation.

proof.text: The image $A=\rho(R)$ is a Lie subalgebra of $\operatorname{End}_F(M)$, because $R$ is bracket-closed and $\rho$ preserves brackets. For $u,v\in R$ we have $\operatorname{Tr}_M(\rho(u)\rho(v))=B_\rho(u,v)=0$. Thus trace vanishes on all of $A\times A$, in particular on $[A,A]\times A$. Apply [lem-sfb-cartan-trace-criterion-characteristic-zero], with the given characteristic-zero field $F$ and finite-dimensional space $M$, to conclude that $A$ is solvable.

source.place: §22c, printed p.475, The Casimir operator, paragraph applying Cartan criterion to the kernel of the trace form of a faithful representation.

proof.text: By induction on $j$, linearity and bracket preservation give $\rho(D^jR)=D^jA$: this is the definition of $A$ for $j=0$, and taking linear spans of brackets proves the successor case [def-wf-lie-algebra]. Choose $j$ with $D^jA=0$. Injectivity of $\rho$ then gives $D^jR=0$, so $R$ is solvable. Since $R$ is an ideal and $L$ has no nonzero solvable ideal [def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra], $R=0$. Every $x$ orthogonal to all of $L$ belongs to $R$ and is therefore zero, as required.
